sections.html:
Douglas County hugs the Columbia River in north-central Washington. The seat is Waterville, though East Wenatchee has the most people, and the county is counted in the Wenatchee metro area. Three cities (Bridgeport, East Wenatchee and Rock Island) and several towns share the land. The city or town your parcel falls in matters at sale time, because the local excise tax rate depends on location.

The 2020 count was 42,938 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 46,473. Of 17,318 housing units in 2020, 11.0% were vacant, and owners lived in 70.7% of the occupied ones.

sections.h2: Offices that handle Douglas County property tax
sections.html:
Four separate offices touch your tax: Assessor, Treasurer, Auditor and Board of Equalization. Most sit on South Rainier Street in Waterville.

  • Assessor: 213 S Rainier Street, mailing address P.O. Box 387, Waterville. Phone 509-745-8521. The counter is staffed weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Treasurer: in the same building, mailing address P.O. Box 609. Call 509-745-8525. Excise tax on sales and tax foreclosures also run through this desk.
  • Auditor: records deeds. Call 509-745-8527.
  • Board of Equalization: 203 S Rainier, Waterville, P.O. Box 747. Call 509-745-8537.

The Treasurer also bills under contract for five irrigation districts, so your statement may include irrigation charges on top of the property tax.

sections.h2: How the Assessor values a house
sections.html:
Every parcel is valued at 100% of market value, as Washington law requires, and Douglas County redoes every value each year. When a number looks wrong, ring 509-745-8521 first and walk the appraiser through what you see. That route can fix a simple record error without a hearing.

Relief programs mostly turn on age and income. The senior exemption may fit residents 61 or older, people who retired because of disability, and a veteran with a qualifying disability, with household income deciding. The Assessor's page links a screening tool, but staff make the final call. Farmland may qualify for open space treatment, and the office also has forms for current use, combining parcels, destroyed property and address changes.

Property tax funds cities, the county, fire protection, law enforcement, libraries, parks, roads and schools. Which of these your parcel pays depends on where it sits.

sections.h2: Due dates, fees and late charges
sections.html:
Your bill comes due in two installments, April 30 and October 31. In 2026 October 31 landed on a Saturday, and a Monday payment dated November 2 raised a question, so check with the Treasurer on how a weekend deadline is treated if you are cutting it close. If you miss the first installment, the full year's tax becomes delinquent under RCW 84.56.020, with interest figured monthly.

To pay, phone Point and Pay at 866-898-2916 or use the TaxSifter parcel search online. A payment must be processed before 11:59 p.m. Pacific time to count for that day, yet it is not posted in real time, so budget two to three business days. Vendor fees: a flat $2.30 for eCheck, 2.7% for credit cards and 0.95% for debit. The Personal Teller live-agent service adds $5.

Residential property with four units or fewer owes 9% a year and no penalties. Other property owes 12% a year plus penalties of 3% and then 8%.

The county commissioners make up the Board of Equalization. They bring in an independent hearing examiner to conduct hearings and recommend outcomes, and the board and its clerk stay separate from the Assessor.

A finished petition must be in by July 1 of the assessment year. If your Change of Value Notice was mailed later, you instead get 30 days from the mailing date. Whichever date is later controls, and the filing must be filed or postmarked by it.

  • Email: BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US, received by 5 p.m.
  • Mail: Douglas County Board of Equalization, P.O. Box 747, Waterville, WA 98858.
  • In person: Public Service Building, 140 19th Street NW, East Wenatchee.

Do not hold back payment while an appeal is pending. If the value is lowered, the county credits your account with the difference. The county also has a waiver of late filing request form, and a late petition can sometimes be excused for good cause.

Nearly every sale in Washington carries real estate excise tax, and WAC 458-61A-301 puts it on the seller. The Treasurer takes it in as the state's agent. Bring the sale in within 30 days of the sale date or interest and penalties start.

The order of stops matters: Treasurer with the excise tax affidavit and deed, then the Auditor for recording. Count on 10 to 20 minutes per document, a first come first served line, and a 4 p.m. cutoff for recording. Title companies and attorneys can skip the trip and file through Simplifile. Courthouse staff cannot write or review a deed, and mobile or manufactured home sales have special requirements, so call 509-745-8525 before you go.

The state portion is added to the local rate and graduates with price. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 follow the Department of Revenue schedule: 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000 and 3% above.

What to bring to the courthouse: the signed deed, the completed excise tax affidavit, and the parcel number. Mobile or manufactured home sales need extra paperwork, so ask first.

Unpaid taxes can end in foreclosure, since the Treasurer is legally required to seize and sell delinquent property. Short of that, the state lets the Treasurer set up payment agreements and take partial payments, oldest year first. A low-income owner who lives in the house may request a waiver of interest and penalties once the parcel is facing foreclosure, beginning 60 days ahead of the third anniversary of delinquency.

Phone 509-745-8525 for a payoff figure before you pick a closing date. Because interest accrues monthly, last month's number may fall short. Give the final amount to your title company, which will pay the lien from your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer needs no lender approval, which can help when a payoff deadline is near.

A simple order of steps: get the payoff figure, confirm the local excise rate for your city, gather the deed and affidavit, and give the Treasurer the sale within the 30-day window. Doing the property tax payoff and the excise filing together keeps the county's records clean for the buyer.

faqs.q: When are Douglas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31. If the first installment is missed, the whole year's tax is delinquent.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Douglas County appeal?
faqs.a: Email BOE@CO.DOUGLAS.WA.US by 5 p.m., mail it to P.O. Box 747, Waterville, or bring it to the Public Service Building at 140 19th Street NW in East Wenatchee. File by July 1, or within 30 days of your notice if that is later.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Douglas County taxes by card?
faqs.a: The vendor charges 2.7% on credit and 0.95% on debit. An eCheck is a flat $2.30.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax rate in East Wenatchee?
faqs.a: East Wenatchee's local rate is 0.50%, and the state's price-based rate comes on top of it.

faqs.q: Does Douglas County offer a senior property tax exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners 61 or older, people retired because of a disability, and a veteran with a qualifying disability, depending on household income. Call the Assessor at 509-745-8521.
